facts.statement: The fossil material of Ptychotherates was discovered in 1982 at the Coelophysis Quarry in Ghost Ranch, New Mexico.
facts.quote: The Ptychotherates fossil material was discovered in the Coelophysis Quarry at Ghost Ranch, northern New Mexico, United States in 1982.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Ptychotherates is housed at the Carnegie Museum of Natural History in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, with accession number CM 31368.
facts.quote: The specimen is housed in the Carnegie Museum of Natural History in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, where it is permanently accessioned as specimen CM 31368.

facts.statement: The genus Ptychotherates contains only one known species, Ptychotherates bucculentus, which is known from a partial skull.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Ptychotherates bucculentus, known from a partial skull.

facts.statement: Ptychotherates possesses a jugal bone that is unusually tall and deeper than in any other known Triassic dinosaur.
facts.quote: The jugal bone of the skull is unusually tall, deeper than in any other Triassic dinosaur.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen consists of a nearly complete but somewhat disarticulated skull.
facts.quote: The specimen consists of a nearly complete, albeit somewhat disarticulated, skull.

facts.statement: The generic name Ptychotherates is derived from Greek words meaning 'fold' and 'hunter'.
facts.quote: The generic name, Ptychotherates, combines the Greek words ptycho, meaning fold and therates, meaning hunter.

facts.statement: The specific name bucculentus means 'with full cheeks' in Latin, referring to the species' tall jugal bone.
facts.quote: The specific name, bucculentus, is a Latin word meaning with full cheeks, referring to the species' unusually tall jugal.

facts.statement: Ptychotherates is classified as a saurischian dinosaur belonging to the novel clade Morphoraptora.
facts.quote: A saurischian in the novel clade Morphoraptora.

facts.statement: Ptychotherates is closely related to Chindesaurus, Daemonosaurus, and Tawa, forming the clade Morphoraptora within the group Herrerasauria.
facts.quote: Ptychotherates is closely related to Chindesaurus, Daemonosaurus, and Tawa, together forming the clade Morphoraptora within Herrerasauria.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses place Ptychotherates within Herrerasauria, in a clade with Chindesaurus, Daemonosaurus, and Tawa.
facts.quote: Both recovered Ptychotherates within the Herrerasauria, in a clade alongside Chindesaurus, Daemonosaurus, and Tawa.

facts.statement: Ptychotherates lived during the Late Triassic, specifically the Norian or Rhaetian ages.
The type locality for Ptychotherates is the Chinle Formation.
Ptychotherates is known from the Chinle Formation at Ghost Ranch, New Mexico, United States.
facts.quote: Ptychotherates () is an extinct genus of saurischian dinosaur known from the Late Triassic (Norian or Rhaetian ages) Chinle Formation of Ghost Ranch, New Mexico, United States.

facts.statement: The time range for Ptychotherates is estimated to be between 205.7 and 201.4 million years ago during the Rhaetian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Rhaetian to Rhaetian (205.7 to 201.4 million years ago)

facts.statement: Ptychotherates shares synapomorphies with Tawa hallae, including distinctive fossae on the quadrate and otoccipital bones and a dorsoventrally tall, laterally flat jugal.
Ptychotherates is distinguished from other coeval ornithodirans by having the proportionally deepest jugal known for any Triassic-aged dinosaur.

rejected.statement: Ptychotherates was described as a new genus and species in 2026 by Simba Srivastava and Sterling J. Nesbitt.
rejected.quote: In 2026, Simba Srivastava and Sterling J. Nesbitt described Ptychotherates bucculentus as a new genus and species of saurischian dinosaur based on these fossil remains.
